Subject: Post-call: MAP next steps & draft Tech Eval milestone

Hi Sam - great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Call highlights:
- Use case: customer support summarization + RAG for internal KB; priority is response latency for live chat and accurate retrieval.
- Success criteria (high level): comparable helpfulness to current baseline, <300ms p95 latency for single-request inference, and predictable unit cost.
- Technical contacts: you mentioned Priya Mehta (ML Eng) will lead the evaluation; please confirm.

Proposed MAP milestone (Technical evaluation plan):
1) Agree dataset & scope (sample logs + 50 canonical prompts) - owner: Acme (Priya) - due: 2026-06-30
2) Redwood to run benchmark run + shortlist models & quantization profiles - owner: Redwood (Rishi + Marissa) - due: 2026-07-15
3) Joint POC (end-to-end integration, latency & cost measurement) - owner: Acme + Redwood - target complete: 2026-07-30
4) Decision & commercial discussion - target close: 2026-08-01

Ask: can you confirm Priya as the technical lead and confirm the week of 6/22 for a short sync with her to agree dataset access? I've attached a first-pass MAP spreadsheet and a short benchmarks spec.

Attachments: Acme_MAP_Milestone_TechEval_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), benchmarks-specs.md (benchmark and metric definitions)

Thanks - I'll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@acme.com>, Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@acme.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-21T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft: Technical Evaluation Plan (details & model shortlist)

Hi Sam & Priya - thanks for the quick reply and for joining. Per our discussion, I'm sharing a first-pass MAP milestone focused on the Technical Evaluation. Below is the draft milestone text - I've kept owners and deliverables explicit so we can drop into the MAP spreadsheet (attached).

---
Milestone: Technical evaluation plan (POC + benchmarks)
Target completion: 2026-07-30
Owners: Acme (Priya Mehta) - dataset + integration; Redwood (Marissa Cole, Rishi Malhotra) - benchmark harness, model shortlist, infra config
Dependencies: dataset access (S3 link / sample export), VPN or secure upload, test keys for Redwood staging environment
Deliverables:
- Benchmark run results (latency, cost, quality metrics) for shortlisted models
- Integration notes and recommended config (batching, kv cache, quantization profile)
- Final recommendation with fallback model options and expected unit economics
Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for single-request live-chat flow (batch=1) in Redwood staging under expected PoC concurrency
- Cost: inference cost < $0.40 per 1k output tokens (end-to-end including batching/overheads)
- Quality: retrieval recall@5 >= 0.85 on the provided sample set; summarization quality >= baseline as judged by agreed rubric (we will provide rubric examples)

Model shortlist (initial):
- Llama-3-70B (8k context) - q4_0 / q8_0 baseline runs
- OpenAssistant-13B (fine-tuned conversational) - q4_0
- Mistral-Instruct-30B (if latency allows) - q4_0 / int8 where available
- Redwood-curated distilled model (small) as a low-cost fallback

Benchmark plan (high level):
1) Small-scale correctness & quality runs on public-staging data (Rishi)
2) Latency profiling with single-request and small batch sizes, measuring p50/p95/p99 the same env as PoC
3) Cost modeling across observed token rates and recommended batching settings

Attachments: Acme_MAP_Milestone_TechEval_v1.xlsx, benchmarks-specs.md

Next steps: Priya, if you confirm dataset readiness and availability for a 6/30 handoff, we'll schedule the 6/23 sync to finalize access details and then kick off the benchmark work the week of 6/29.

Thanks - I'll also add a HubSpot note with the MAP and the timeline.

Best,
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft: Technical Evaluation Plan (internal alignment)

Quick internal alignment - looping in a few technical details we should own prior to the Priya sync:

1) Benchmark success criteria (concrete):
- Latency: p95 < 300ms (batch=1) for the staging configuration; measure under target PoC concurrency (TBD by Acme)
- Throughput: baseline target 50 concurrent low-latency requests for PoC; adjust if Acme provides different expected concurrency
- Cost: modeled inference cost < $0.40 per 1k output tokens (include overheads like batching inefficiency and network egress where applicable)
- Quality: retrieval recall@5 >= 0.85; for summarization we'll use a small human-eval sample (10 seed cases) + automated ROUGE-L for initial triage

2) Model & infra notes:
- Start with Llama-3-70B q4_0 for a performance baseline and an OpenAssistant-13B for a smaller footprint comparison. If L3-70B latency is too high on our reserved instance type, test Mistral-30B for middle-ground latency.
- Prepare quantization profiles (q4_0 and q8_0 where supported) and a distilled small model as fallback.
- KV-cache/streaming test: ensure we exercise typical chat-turn lengths (avg 120 tokens) and regen scenarios so caching behavior is realistic.

3) Deliverables & runbook items for the PoC:
- Benchmark harness repo link (internal) + run script for reproducibility
- Measurement sheet that logs model, quant profile, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens out/in, and cost estimate per 1k tokens
- Quick triage checklist for unexpected regressions (quality or latency) and recommended fallback policy (auto-failover to smaller distilled model)

I'll prepare the initial benchmark harness and a template run on Monday so we can demo sample numbers to Priya in the sync. Marissa - let me know if you want me on the 6/23 sync.

-Rishi
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
